job.title: Clinical Manager, Aged Care - Wellington Central
job.description:
Are you a proven Clinical Manager or a Registered Nurse with solid people management skills, based in Wellington or considering a move, with the type of personality that resonates and motivates people?  Want to work for a leader in the retirement village sector, one that invests in its people and puts the welfare of its residents first? We would urge you to consider this career option.

We are seeking a strong and natural leader to join our senior leadership team as we work together to foster a care delivery culture that supports the values and purpose of our aged community. 

If you are passionate about measurable and meaningful quality of care that meets contractual and legislative requirements and reflects current best practices, this is the opportunity for you.

You will lead a passionate team committed to supporting our aged care residents to live life their way.

This is a full-time role working Monday to Friday with some on-call requirements during evenings and weekends.

Qualifications
Our ideal candidate must have
  • At least 5 years of experience working as a registered nurse with a passion for aged care (and a current NZ annual practicing certificate).
  • Be committed to holistic person-centered care.
  • Have a calm and measured approach - able to problem-solve and adapt to an ever-changing environment.
  • Be an effective and respectful communicator; highly skilled in written, oral, and interpersonal communication. 
  • Be able to build strong relationships with your team, residents, and whanau
  • Have experience with leading a team, including recruitment and development of staff and managing rosters.
  • Have strong organisational and time management skills.
  • Be InterRAI trained.
  • Engage with all our professional stakeholders to build strong local relationships.
  • Be resilient and committed to self-care.
What's on offer
  • A competitive market rate
  • An engaging and positive work environment
  • Ongoing professional development
  • Professional supervision
  • To become a part of the nationwide village community
  • Support to complete post-graduate study
  • A great local leadership team and ongoing mentorship
If you are looking for a role with a real sense of purpose and the opportunity to genuinely make a difference, this is the role for you! Please use the APPLY NOW button to progress your application or call Kirsten Edwards, Farrow Jamieson on +64 9 915 9140 for a confidential chat.

job.title: GM Village Operations
job.description:
About the Company

Freedom Lifestyle Villages is a New Zealand operator of fully managed, over-50s lifestyle communities. Its villages are designed around independent living, modern low-maintenance homes, resident-led community life and a differentiated financial model that allows residents to participate in capital gains, subject to the relevant village terms.
As the business enters its next phase of growth, Freedom is focused on strengthening village leadership and delivering a consistently positive resident experience across its national portfolio. Sound commercial management, safe operations and practical systems will support that ambition.

About the Role

Reporting to the CEO and based in Tauranga with relevant travel, you will lead seven Village Managers across Freedom’s operating portfolio. Your impact will come through the people you lead and continue growing: giving village leaders clear direction, coaching them through challenges and helping their teams deliver the service and community experience residents expect.
You will listen to residents and frontline teams, turn their insight into practical improvements, and build a consistent approach across villages while respecting what makes each community distinct. You will also be accountable for portfolio performance, safety, compliance and the operating foundations needed for growth.

What You Will Do
  • Lead, coach and support Village Managers, building their confidence, capability and accountability.
  • Set clear expectations for resident care, communication and service, then help teams turn those expectations into everyday practice.
  • Use resident feedback, frontline insight and operational data to identify improvements and follow through on them.
  • Support Village Managers with complex or sensitive resident matters, balancing empathy, fairness and sound judgement.
  • Strengthen a collaborative culture across villages, encouraging shared learning, recognition and consistent standards.
  • Set the village operations strategy, annual plans and portfolio priorities, with a clear focus on resident outcomes.
  • Lead budgets, forecasts, capital planning and commercial performance so villages have the resources and discipline to deliver well.
  • Establish practical policies, workflows, controls and reporting that make it easier for teams to do their jobs well.
  • Provide leadership across Health and Safety, compliance, risk, village services, facilities, maintenance and suppliers.
  • Report clearly to the CEO, Senior Leadership Team and Board, and identify useful technology and AI applications that improve service and operations.
What You Bring
  • Senior leadership experience across multiple sites, ideally in retirement living, property, accommodation, hospitality, healthcare or another regulated service environment.
  • A track record of coaching managers, building engaged teams and achieving results through others.
  • Strong judgement, empathy and communication skills in resident, customer or community-facing settings.
  • The ability to listen, handle sensitive issues constructively and turn feedback into better service.
  • Commercial acumen across budgets, forecasts, cost control, capital priorities and performance improvement.
  • Experience creating consistent, scalable ways of working across multiple sites, together with sound Health and Safety, compliance and risk leadership.
  • Confidence using data and technology, including practical AI applications, to improve decisions, productivity and the resident experience.
Culture and Leadership

Freedom’s purpose is to empower lifestyle freedom for over-50s living. Its values emphasise working as One Team, doing the right thing, making it happen, being brave and keeping it real.
You will be a visible, approachable leader who earns trust with Village Managers, their teams and residents. You will combine warmth and fairness with clear expectations, support people to grow, and work across functions to make improvements stick.

Why Join Freedom
  • Make a direct difference to residents’ experience across a growing national village portfolio.
  • Coach seven Village Managers and develop leadership capability across their teams.
  • Help shape the operating culture, service standards and next phase of growth.
  • Hold a senior leadership role with influence over commercial performance and cross-functional decisions.
  • Be based in Tauranga, with relevant travel across the village portfolio.
How to Apply

For a confidential discussion, contact Iain MacGibbon at Farrow Jamieson on +64 9 915 9144 or Rosemary MacGibbon on 029 520 4754. To apply, click the “APPLY” button and submit your CV and relevant details.

job.title: National Commercial Manager
job.description:
National Commercial Manager - Own national sales growth, major accounts and commercial strategy

About the Company
Our client is a fast-growing, New Zealand-wide B2B services business operating in a demanding, operationally intensive environment. Continued growth has created the need for stronger commercial leadership, sharper pipeline discipline and deeper national customer relationships.

This is an energetic, hands-on business where commercial success is closely connected to operational delivery. What gets sold needs to be delivered well, and customer relationships have to be earned every day.

About the Role
Based in Auckland and reporting to the General Manager, you will take national ownership of revenue growth, gross profit, customer retention, pipeline, key accounts and sales performance. You will lead a small Auckland-based Client Services/Sales team while influencing regional and operational leaders across New Zealand.

This is not a sit-behind-a-dashboard sales role. You will set direction, coach the team, stay close to the numbers and still be prepared to pick up the phone, get in front of customers and chase the next opportunity. It is an ideal step for an experienced sales leader - or a high-performing BDM ready for a broader national leadership remit.

Responsibilities
• Own national revenue, gross profit and customer retention targets, with clear accountability for results.
• Build and manage a disciplined forward pipeline, looking several months ahead.
• Hunt new business, open doors and convert opportunities into sustainable revenue.
• Grow major accounts through regular contact, strong service and proactive relationship management.
• Lead commercial planning, forecasting and performance reporting, using the numbers to identify opportunities and address gaps.
• Lead, coach and hold the Client Services/Sales team accountable for performance.
• Influence regional and operational leaders to align sales activity with delivery capability.
• Manage pricing, rate cards, customer mix and margins to protect profitability.
• Represent the business in major client reviews, commercial negotiations, networking and industry events.
• Support tenders, major client onboarding, key projects and service-improvement initiatives.
• Travel regularly across New Zealand, with occasional client-hosting events outside standard hours.

Skills & Experience
• A strong B2B sales or business development track record, with clear evidence of winning new revenue and growing major accounts.
• Experience leading or coaching a sales/client-facing team - or clear readiness to step into broader national leadership responsibility.
• Strong commercial and financial capability across budgets, forecasting, financial modelling, pricing, margins and performance reporting.
• High EQ, strong negotiation skills and the ability to build genuine relationships with a wide range of personalities.
• A hands-on hunting mindset: you are comfortable networking, prospecting, cold-contacting and staying close to customers.
• Experience in utilities, water, power, infrastructure, labour hire, equipment hire, uniforms/workwear or another high-volume B2B service environment would translate well.
• You will ideally understand businesses where work must be continually won rather than simply secured through long-term contracts.
• Sector-specific experience is not essential. Transferable commercial capability, leadership potential and fit matter more.

Culture
The environment is high-energy, ambitious and practical. Leaders are expected to take ownership, keep momentum and work closely across functions rather than operate in silos.

The right person will be commercially driven without being overly “salesy”. You will know how to build trust, influence others and follow opportunities through to delivery. You will also enjoy the pace of a business where no two days look quite the same.

Benefits
• Take ownership of a genuinely national commercial remit.
• Work directly with an ambitious senior leadership team and influence growth strategy.
• Join a business in a strong growth phase where your impact will be highly visible.
• Combine strategic leadership with real customer contact and hands-on business development.
• Bring transferable experience from a broad range of B2B service industries.

How to Apply
If you are a commercially driven sales leader who still enjoys the chase - winning work, developing people and building long-term customer relationships - click the “APPLY” button to submit your application.

For a confidential discussion, contact Amanda Campbell at Farrow Jamieson on +64 9 915 9142

job.title: Care Home Manager - Auckland Central
job.description:
The Company

A well-established and highly regarded aged-care provider is seeking an experienced Care Home Manager to lead one of its Auckland care homes. Providing hospital-level and dementia care, the care home is focused on delivering high-quality clinical care and creating a safe, supportive environment for residents.

About the Role

As Care Home Manager, you will have overall responsibility for the care home's leadership and operations, ensuring high standards of clinical care, compliance, and service delivery, alongside strong operational performance and an engaged team culture.

This is a hands-on leadership role requiring a visible, supportive leader who can bring people together, maintain high clinical standards, and ensure the home operates effectively.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the day-to-day operation of the care home, ensuring a safe, welcoming and high-quality environment.
  • Maintain strong clinical standards across hospital-level and dementia care.
  • Lead quality, compliance and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Oversee budgets, occupancy, staffing and resource planning.
  • Build strong relationships with residents, families, staff and the wider community.
  • Recruit, coach and develop a high-performing multidisciplinary team.
  • Maintain your RN competency and provide clinical leadership and oversight as required.
What We’re Looking For
  • Current NZ Registered Nurse with a valid APC.
  • Proven leadership experience within aged residential care.
  • Experience within hospital-level and/or dementia care environments.
  • Strong understanding of aged-care standards, quality systems and compliance.
  • Sound operational and financial management capability.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to lead teams, manage change and build a positive workplace culture.
  • Commitment to culturally safe care and working effectively with diverse communities.
The Offer

This is an opportunity to lead a substantial and well-supported aged-care facility in Auckland. You will join an experienced wider leadership team and have the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to the quality of care, team culture and day-to-day experience of residents and their families.

A competitive remuneration package and ongoing professional development are offered.

Apply Now

Please use the APPLY NOW button to submit your application or contact Kirsten Edwards on +64 9 915 9140 for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Executive Recruitment Consultant
job.description:
About the Company

Farrow Jamieson is an executive search and recruitment firm with more than 40 years in the New Zealand market. We are part of the Alpha Group of Companies, which include, Sheffield South Island, Emergent, The Johnson Group, Project Plus, Manamahi, Asset Recruitment, Alpha Recruitment, Triangle Recruitment, Healthwise Personnel and Staffwise.
We have built our longevity on a willingness to keep changing: adopting the best technology we can find globally, testing new approaches and continually improving how we identify and attract talent. Technology matters to us, but people matter more. We never lose sight of the fact that recruitment deals with people's careers, hopes and aspirations.

About  the Role
This is an opportunity for a Recruitment Consultant who wants to become more skilled, effective and commercially capable. You may currently work in a specialist discipline or as a generalist; what matters is your appetite to listen, change, grow and contribute to the team.

You will manage recruitment assignments, build trusted client and candidate relationships, and use contemporary technology and search methods to identify and engage the right people.
Duties
  • Manage recruitment assignments from briefing through to successful appointment.
    • Build enduring relationships with clients and understand what success looks like for them.
    • Identify, approach and engage high-quality candidates using modern search tools and technology.
    • Represent candidates thoughtfully, recognising the importance of career decisions.
    • Contribute ideas, knowledge and effort to the wider Farrow Jamieson team.
    • Keep developing your craft and look for better, faster and more effective ways to work.
Skills & Experience
We are interested in recruitment professionals who can demonstrate:

• Recruitment experience in a specialist discipline or generalist environment.
• Strong listening, communication and relationship-building skills.
• A genuine commitment to client satisfaction and high-quality work.
• Curiosity about technology and new ways of identifying and attracting talent.
• The capacity to accept feedback, change approach and keep developing.
Culture

Farrow Jamieson people do not talk about “hot desks”, “rock stars” or “ninjas”. We talk about client satisfaction, doing great work and enjoying the success that follows.

We are a supportive team that values professional judgement, continuous improvement and shared success. Our expectation is for people to commit to the team as well as their own performance.
Benefits
  • Grow your recruitment career in a supportive, professional, experienced team environment.
    • Use leading technology, sourced globally, to make search and engagement more effective.
    • Join a long-established national firm that continues to evolve.
    • Develop management and leadership skills within Farrow Jamieson or the wider Alpha Group of Companies.
    • Build deeper capability across client management, search, candidate engagement and recruitment delivery.
How to Apply
If you call, be ready to answer two questions: How do you know recruitment is what you want to do as a career? And can you convince us that you will listen, grow and contribute to a highly professional team.

Still want to talk? Click the “APPLY” button to submit your application. For a confidential discussion, contact Iain MacGibbon at Farrow Jamieson on +64 9 915 9144.
